newsitem.title: JAPAN: EXIM Japan, IMF in $8 bln Thai loan plan-daily.
newsitem.headline: EXIM Japan, IMF in $8 bln Thai loan plan-daily.

text.p: The Export-Import Bank of Japan and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have put together an $8 billion emergency loan package for beleaguered Thailand, a Japanese financial newspaper reported on Sunday.
Japan's private banks would coordinate several billion dollars in additional loans to help Bangkok shore up its foreign reserves and restructure its economy, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
The plan would be unveiled by the EXIM after August 5, when Thailand was set to unveil a restructuring plan to meet IMF lending conditions and request loans from Japan, it said.
The loan scheme would be implemented as early as the latter half of August, the newspaper said.

Private Japanese banks, including Sakura Bank Ltd, and Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, would lead efforts by U.S. and European banks which have offices in Thailand, and Southeast Asian banks to extend several billion in additional loans, the report said.

Japanese media reported on Friday the private sector banks' loan package would likely be dispersed in late September, when the IMF and the World Bank are due to hold their annual joint meeting in Hong Kong.
Officials from EXIM Japan, Japan's Ministry of Finance and the private banks could not be reached for comment on the plan.
In response to reports of a Thai bailout scheme earlier this week, the Ministry of Finance and several of the banks said no decisions could be taken while Bangkok was still negotiating with the IMF.
